cards.headline: Lamine Yamal stays in Barcelona with mild right-ankle discomfort and misses Sabah
cards.summary:
FC Barcelona confirmed on Monday that Lamine Yamal will not travel to Baku. The club said the 19-year-old is experiencing mild discomfort in his right ankle and, as a precaution, will miss Wednesday’s Champions League match against Sabah.

He played the full 90 minutes in Sunday’s 3-2 comeback win over Villarreal. The statement added that he is expected to be available for next Sunday’s La Liga trip to Deportivo. Yamal has started all 17 of Barça’s matches this season.

cards.headline: Squad lands in Baku after the longest European trip in the club’s history
cards.summary:
The Barça expedition, led by president Joan Laporta, arrived in Baku on Monday evening after a flight of roughly four hours and twenty minutes. The distance is about 3,970 kilometres, the longest European journey the club has ever made.

Around 400 people welcomed the party at the private terminal. Raphinha, Pedri, De Jong and Hansi Flick drew the loudest reception. The group moved to the Ritz-Carlton. Yamal remained in Barcelona with the ankle issue.

cards.headline: Flick names a 22-man squad that includes Bisiwu and leaves Yamal at home
cards.summary:
Hansi Flick took 22 players to Azerbaijan. Goalkeepers Joan García, Wojciech Szczęsny and Dominik Livaković travel. The defence has Cancelo, Balde, Cubarsí, Gerard Martín, Koundé, Eric García and Àlex Campos.

Midfield and attack list Pedri, Gavi, De Jong, Bernal, Fermín López, Fariñas, Olmo, Raphinha, Gabriel Jesus, Adeyemi, Gordon and Jesse Bisiwu. Absent are Yamal, Hamza, Christensen, Espart, Bardghji and Rodri. Bisiwu earns his first senior call-up.

cards.headline: Jesse Bisiwu receives his first official first-team call-up for the Sabah trip
cards.summary:
Eighteen-year-old Belgian winger Jesse Bisiwu travels with the senior squad for the first time in an official competition. He joined from Club Brugge in the summer for around €8.5 million and has been playing with Barça Atlètic in the Segunda Federación.

SPORT reported that the call-up fills the gap left by Yamal and Hamza. Bisiwu has started all eight of his reserve appearances this season. Flick had already given him first-team minutes in pre-season, including two goals against Basel.

cards.headline: Cubarsí travels after the psoas issue; Christensen, Espart and Rodri stay out
cards.summary:
Pau Cubarsí is among the 22 players who flew to Baku. He had been managing a minor iliopsoas overload and remained on the bench against Villarreal. Andreas Christensen is still missing with the left soleus problem that will keep him out for two matches.

Xavi Espart and Rodri also remain unavailable. The back line options in Azerbaijan therefore centre on Cubarsí, Eric García, Gerard Martín and Koundé, with Cancelo and Balde covering the flanks.

cards.headline: Fermín López travels to Baku but faces a ban for the Deportivo match
cards.summary:
Fermín López is part of the 22-man squad that landed in Baku. He scored the equaliser against Villarreal on 61 minutes before being shown a red card from the bench in the 74th minute for protesting to the fourth official.

Mundo Deportivo reported that the referee’s report cited repeated use of the phrase “No me jodas”. A two-match suspension would rule him out of Sunday’s visit to Deportivo and the rearranged league game against Atlético on 2 December. The club is expected to appeal.

cards.headline: Official accounts post the arrival: Hello, Baku and long-flight images
cards.summary:
FC Barcelona’s English account posted “Hello, Baku” with video of the landing. The Spanish account followed with “Hemos aterrizado en Bakú”. Earlier posts showed the departure from Barcelona and the length of the flight.

The club also published the full squad list under the hashtag #SabahBarça. A later image showed Raphinha ready for the Champions League. The posts marked the halfway point of the league phase, with Barça fifth on nine points after three wins and one defeat.

cards.headline: Training set for 17:00 local time on Tuesday at the Baku Olympic Stadium
cards.summary:
Because of the five-hour flight and the three-hour time difference, the squad will not train on Monday. Hansi Flick has scheduled the session for Tuesday at 17:00 local time at the Baku Olympic Stadium, the venue for Wednesday’s match.

Flick and one player will face the media 45 minutes before the session. Kick-off against Sabah is Wednesday at 18:45 Spanish time (21:45 local). A win would strengthen Barça’s position in the race for a top-eight finish.

cards.headline: Barça sit fifth in the Champions League league phase heading into the Sabah match
cards.summary:
After three wins and a defeat in the opening four matches of the league phase, Barça are fifth on nine points. Sabah occupy 31st place with three points.

Wednesday’s fixture is the longest trip of the season and the first of four remaining league-phase games. Flick has already flagged the need to manage minutes. The next league match after the return is the visit to Deportivo on 29 November, with Yamal expected back.
